The view has only `@login_required` (line 1168) with no role check. Any authenticated user including patients can query any provider's future schedule. The response (line 1200+) returns all available time slots, revealing provider availability patterns (busy periods). While no direct PHI is leaked, schedule enumeration can reveal appointment density and practice patterns.

extra.message: Import appointments allows arbitrary status assignment via CSV column bypassing workflow

metadata.proof: SOURCE: User-uploaded CSV `status` column -> SINK: `Appointment.objects.create(..., status=row.get('status', 'scheduled'))` (line 1062). The import endpoint allows front_desk and clinic_admin users to set any appointment status directly from the CSV file. An attacker can craft a CSV with `status=completed` to bypass the check-in and complete workflow, or `status=cancelled` to mass-cancel appointments, or `status=checked_in` to bypass the normal check-in process.

An attacker can script requests to enumerate valid accounts in the system by observing the distinct error messages versus success or generic errors for new accounts.

metadata.proof: SOURCE: clinician selects patient via form dropdown -> SINK: `PrescriptionForm` field `patient` (line 170) with unrestricted queryset `PatientProfile.objects.select_related('user')` (line 175) and `prescription_create` view (line 512) never validates patient-provider assignment. The view (`prescription_create`, lines 510-522) checks `is_clinician or is_clinic_admin` but never validates that the selected patient is assigned to the clinician. A clinician can create prescriptions for any patient in the system.

extra.message: BOLA/IDOR: prescription_edit allows clinician to reassign prescription to an unaffiliated patient

metadata.proof: SOURCE: clinician submits edited form including a changed 'patient' field -> SINK: `form = PrescriptionForm(request.POST, instance=rx)` (line 529). The check on line 526 (`rx.provider != request.user.provider_profile`) only validates the ORIGINAL prescription's provider matches the clinician, but never validates the new patient after `form.save()` (line 532). The form's `patient` field queryset is unrestricted (forms.py line 175). A clinician who owns a prescription for Patient A can move it to Patient B (who may not be assigned to them) by submitting an edited patient field.

extra.message: Denial of Service: import_appointments reads entire CSV into memory with no row limit

metadata.proof: SOURCE: attacker uploads an arbitrarily large CSV via POST /import/appointments/ -> SINK: `csv_file.read().decode('utf-8')` (line 1041) materializes the entire file into memory, then `for row in reader` (line 1043) iterates all rows with no maximum count. An attacker can exhaust server memory or CPU by uploading a multi-gigabyte or million-row CSV, degrading service for all users.

extra.message: Denial of Service: export_visit_summaries materializes all matching visit summaries in memory

metadata.proof: SOURCE: authenticated clinician or admin triggers export via POST /export/visit-summaries/ with a wide date range -> SINK: `data = []` (line 1124) then `for s in qs:` (line 1126) appends each visit summary dictionary to `data`, which is serialized with `JsonResponse`. No pagination, no row cap. A broad date range can produce thousands of visit summaries with large `diagnosis`/`care_instructions` text fields, exhausting server memory.

extra.message: IDOR: prescription_detail permits front_desk users to view any patient's prescription details

metadata.proof: SOURCE: front_desk user requests /prescriptions/<uuid:pk>/ -> SINK: `get_object_or_404(Prescription, pk=pk)` (line 493). The authorization block (lines 494-499) only checks `is_patient` and `is_clinician` roles. A front_desk user (`is_staff_role=True`, but neither patient nor clinician) passes both conditionals and can view any prescription's full details: medication_name, dosage, instructions, refills_allowed, and patient identity — all sensitive PHI with no legitimate front-desk need.

extra.message: Missing rate limiting on message_create allows spam and abuse

metadata.proof: Any authenticated user can POST to /messages/create/ repeatedly. The view has no @ratelimit decorator, no throttle check, and no per-user cooldown. An attacker can flood the system with thousands of messages, creating notification spam, filling the database, and degrading performance.

When form.save() is called on line 301, the user-supplied status value is written directly with no validation of allowed state transitions, allowing any staff user to set arbitrary appointment statuses such as 'completed' or 'no_show'.

extra.message: Disabling a user account does not invalidate existing sessions

metadata.proof: user_toggle_active flips is_active and saves but never calls logout on active sessions or deletes session records; a disabled user remains authenticated until their session cookie expires.

extra.message: PHI documents stored unencrypted at rest

metadata.proof: Uploaded patient documents (lab results, insurance cards, clinical documents) are stored via Django's default FileField with no encryption at rest, exposing PHI if the filesystem or storage backend is compromised.
